angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 45,400,686 km at 255.10 pc = 2.38 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94713: distance 255.102 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.043), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 255.102 +/- 10.969 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 4.2005 +/- 0.1053 mas (same row, RUWE 6.80), 39.9 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 65.259 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94713: radius 65.259 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 1578.8 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.07) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 45,400,686 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4507 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94713: effective temperature 4507 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.07) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94713: effective temperature 4507 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.07) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * tet Lyr: spectral type K0II (1989ApJS...71..245K)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * tet Lyr: main object type *, Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * tet Lyr: projected rotation speed 8.6 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 848) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 1.6 from 1995AJ....110.2425L, the median of its 3 spectra; the 8 published values span log g 1.6 to 1.93, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1995AJ....110.2425L)
